---
description: Generate tasks.md and one DEV artifact per logical plan component.
agent: agent
---

Require one explicit GitHub Development Planning issue reference, either an
issue number or URL. If it is missing, stop immediately and ask the
Development Lead for the issue number. Do not search for, infer, or select an
issue.

Verify that the issue exists, is a Development Planning work order with the
`development` label, identifies exactly one approved `plan.md`, and is
activated at `Ready / Ready for Planning`. Stop and report any missing
prerequisite. Select exactly one mode.

## Prepare mode

Use this mode when `--submit` is absent. Read only the approved plan,
repository/spec/plan contexts, component taxonomy, required payloads, and
`component_task_profiles`. Read and validate `.d365/authoring-targets.yml`;
read and validate `.d365/development-resources.yml`;
the approved plan context already contains the compiler-resolved
`implementation_scope`, `execution_host`, and `authoring_target`.

For every current plan component, resolve `component_type` through
`conventions.yml` `component_type_skills` to exactly one build skill. Invoke
that skill from the registered D365 Solution Craft
`.github/skills/build/<build-skill>/SKILL.md` location and read the
component-specific reference selected by its `SKILL.md`. Apply that guidance
when defining the DEV payload, target roots, validations, acceptance checks,
evidence, and checkpoints. Loading only the task profile or relying on recalled
skill guidance is prohibited. Stop and report the component, type, mapped skill,
and expected Craft path if any mapped skill or required reference is
unavailable.

Generate `.specify/context/task-context.json`, the same workspace's `tasks.md`,
and exactly one authoritative `development/DEV-####.md` per current logical,
typed plan component. Each DEV artifact contains the complete implementation
of that component, including its subordinate fields, properties, steps, child
configuration, and metadata. Preserve completed historical DEV artifacts and
allocate new IDs only for new components.

Copy the resolved implementation scope, execution host, and normalized
authoring target into task context and compiler-owned DEV fields. Display all
three in `tasks.md`. Resolve `local_interactive` for every Dataverse-bound
scope. Resolve `cloud_or_local` for a repository-only task only when every
required routed resource declares GitHub Copilot cloud support; otherwise
resolve `local_interactive`. Keep execution host separate from `executor`.
Copy the compiler-resolved required, preferred, allowed, and fallback
development-resource snapshot into each DEV artifact. Missing, ambiguous, or
unregistered resource routing blocks task generation.
Carry the approved `schema_name` for solution-bound components or `record_name`
for environment-bound components into the compiler-owned DEV payload. The
identity is immutable during task review and is the only allowed lookup key for
implementation; display labels cannot select an update target.
Resolution is automatic and not human-adjustable during task review. Missing,
ambiguous, stale, or scope-incompatible routing blocks task generation; never
invent or substitute a target. Every Dataverse target must retain
`environment_url`, `environment_id`, and
`authentication_mode: interactive_user`; `connection_alias` is optional.
Preserve `CONFIGURE_BEFORE_IMPLEMENTATION` when supplied. It permits planning
but will block Dataverse-bound execution.

Treat manifest-declared custom publishers and unmanaged custom solutions as
administrator-created setup prerequisites. Never generate `alm_publisher` or
`alm_solution` DEV tasks or components. Never generate `alm_managed_export`
tasks; solution export and promotion belong to external pipelines.
`config_queue` and `config_audit`
remain environment-bound composite records and must not claim custom-solution
membership.

Present the component-to-DEV mapping for Development Lead review. Permit human
adjustment of executor (`agent`, `human`, or `hybrid`), owner, declared target
roots, dependencies, validation kinds, acceptance checks, evidence
requirements, and human checkpoints. Explain implications and reconfirm the
complete mapping before recording adjustments.
Do not split a component merely to reduce task size. If the Development Lead
explicitly requests an exceptional split because of independent deployment,
risk, ownership, sequencing, or review needs, record the reason and stop task
submission until the authoritative `plan.md` component boundary is revised and
reviewed. Regenerate the mapping after that revision; never create several DEV
artifacts for one unchanged plan component.
Do not permit adjustment of `implementation_scope`, `execution_host`, authoring environment,
environment URL, environment ID, authentication mode, connection alias, target,
solution, solution unique name, publisher name, or publisher prefix; those
compiler-owned values come only from conventions and the validated
authoring-target contract.

Do not introduce or hide design decisions. Missing payloads, unclear target
roots, an explicitly requested exceptional split, or design ambiguity must
block planning and be routed to the authoritative `plan.md` through a recorded
human decision.
Require one DEV per component, no orphan current components, valid mapped
skills loaded from Craft, component-specific references, exact payloads, and an
acyclic DEV dependency graph. Never generate multiple DEV artifacts that would
add the same logical Dataverse component to different custom solutions.

Run `python scripts/compile_repository_context.py --check`,
`python scripts/validate_authoring_targets.py`,
`python scripts/validate_development_resources.py`,
`python scripts/compile_specs.py --check`,
`python scripts/compile_design.py --check`,
`python scripts/compile_tasks.py`,
`python scripts/compile_tasks.py --check`, and
`python scripts/validate_tasks.py`. Present mapping, assignment, dependency,
checkpoint, and validation summaries, then stop with files uncommitted for
Development Lead review. Do not ask whether to submit. Submission requires a
later explicit `/d365.tasks #<issue-number> --submit` invocation.

## Submit mode

Use this mode only when the invocation contains `--submit`. Treat the explicit
invocation as confirmation that local planning review is complete. Do not
regroup components or alter approved plan intent. Change only in-scope DEV
statuses from `draft` to `ready`; never mark them completed.

Require exact one-to-one current component mapping, complete owners or explicit
human ownership decisions, allowed target roots, valid executors, mapped
skills reloaded from the registered Craft build-skill location,
component-specific references, exact payloads, immutable compiler-resolved
scope, execution-host, and target fields, acceptance and evidence
requirements, completed checkpoint definitions, and an acyclic dependency
graph. Run all upstream checks and task compilation/validation commands from
Prepare mode.

Create a focused branch and stage only the linked workspace's `tasks.md`, its
in-scope `development/DEV-####.md` files, and
`.specify/context/task-context.json`. Never stage `spec.md`, `plan.md`, REQ
files, raw intake documents, implementation output, `audit/`, temporary files,
or unrelated changes. Check the staged diff before committing.

Commit, push, and open one Development Planning PR containing
`Closes #<issue-number>`, plan/feature IDs, component-to-DEV mapping,
executor/owner assignments, target roots, dependencies, checkpoints,
validation results, and an unchecked planning-review checklist. Report an
existing open PR for the same issue and plan instead of creating a duplicate.
Stop before approval or merge.
